title: Sheaves for a generated precoverage are detected on pullback sieves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category [def-weil-size-convention]. A presieve on $X$ is a set of arrows with target $X$; a sieve is a presieve closed under precomposition. Let $J$ be a precoverage, meaning a choice of a set $J(X)$ of presieves on each $X$, with no axioms imposed. For a presieve $R$ on $X$, let $\langle R\rangle$ be the sieve of arrows factoring through an arrow of $R$. Let $J^{\mathrm{gen}}$ be the smallest Grothendieck topology in which $\langle R\rangle$ covers whenever $R\in J(X)$. Let $P:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Set}$ be a presheaf. Then $P$ is a sheaf for $J^{\mathrm{gen}}$ if and only if, for every $R\in J(X)$ and every arrow $f:Y\to X$, every matching family on the sieve $f^*\langle R\rangle=\{g:Z\to Y\mid fg\in\langle R\rangle\}$ has a unique amalgamation in $P(Y)$. Here a matching family on a sieve $S$ on $Y$ is a choice $x_g\in P(Z)$ for every $g:Z\to Y$ in $S$, with $P(h)(x_g)=x_{gh}$ for every $h:W\to Z$; an amalgamation is $x\in P(Y)$ with $P(g)(x)=x_g$ for every $g\in S$. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ are assumed.
